translations.answer: The original comment only provides performance decomposition: LQ Approximation 1528.7 ms, Solve QP 8.36 ms, without confirmation of the root cause or fix. This can be used to focus the investigation on linearization, automatic differentiation models, URDF inertial/kinematics and constraint derivatives, but these are not the original solution provided in the comment.
translations.applicability: Applies to model migration cases with similar OCS2 SQP performance decomposition.
translations.credibility.rationale: The solution has not closed or there is a conflict; the problem is only forming a clue at this point.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author first completed the Cheat Controller, then added and stabilized the linear Kalman state estimator.
translations.details.attempts.1: The inertial and kinematics parameters were re-filled in SolidWorks using the link coordinate system and negative tensor notation.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First, isolate the MPC using an OCS2 dummy, then use the Cheat Controller to directly read simulation truth values and isolate the state estimator.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Check the inertial and kinematics of the URDF, foot end kinematic constraints, and the H matrix weights of the weighted-QP.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: For model migration, use a layered validation approach: dummy → Cheat Controller → state estimator, and correct the inertial parameters.
translations.details.environments.0: MuJoCo simulation; OCS2 NMPC; Pinocchio dynamics; qpOASES weighted-QP WBC; SolidWorks export of URDF.
translations.details.limits.0: The main evidence comes from simulation and the comment section; there is no independent verification of the same process in a real humanoid robot or high-speed motion.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author reported that the simulation framework can run stably; the support leg constraints and the slow LQ Approximation in the SQP have not been reproduced after the fix.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: How can we reduce the difficulty of diagnosing issues when migrating an open-source NMPC+WBC framework to a custom robot model?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why does the framework not retain the static constraint of the support leg?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: After model replacement, the LQ Approximation in OCS2 SQP accounts for 93.5% of the runtime and the dummy robot is stationary.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Incorrect inertial parameters, contact constraints, or state estimation should not be directly deployed on real machines; they should be validated in dummy and simulation first.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The inertial matrix exported by the SolidWorks URDF plugin may be incorrect.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The static support leg constraint was causing issues during the author's debugging and was removed; the root cause of the SQP linearization bottleneck has not been confirmed.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The foot end trajectory is abnormally directed in the custom model; the dummy node does not respond to commands.
translations.details.symptoms.1: A comment measures the LQ Approximation at 1528.7 ms, which accounts for 93.5049% of the total SQP time.
translations.source.locator: The comment section contains a question about SQP Benchmarking
